title: Israel expands eVisa-B2 to 50 more nationalities
summary: The Embassy of Israel in Singapore's notice of 28 October 2026 lists 50 additional nationalities for online B/2 e-Visas (plus India and Sri Lanka from the pilot), and the PIBA portal's public pages as of 31 October 2026 present the e-Visa as open to visa-required countries with no pilot restriction shown; the email-verified form itself was not tested, so the pair notes carry that caveat. The 10 exempt nationalities the notice also names keep their exemption plus ETA-IL.
source_name: PIBA - eVisa-B2 information page

title: Lebanon adopts a new entry standard for Syrian nationals
summary: General Security Notice 572 replaces a single tourist route for Syrian passports with a purpose-by-purpose regime at all air, land and sea ports: pre-booked hotel stay, business visit, property ownership, medical treatment, study and family cases each carry their own stay and papers, and work still requires a Labour Ministry permit plus pre-approval. The announcement was confirmed live by 27 October 2026 (GDGS page crawled that day); the text states no separate gazette day.
source_name: Lebanese General Security, Notice 572 (AR)
State Migration Service of Turkmenistan
summary: Turkmenistan's State Migration Service opened an online e-Visa system on 1 October 2026. The portal's document lists no longer include the invitation letter (LOI) that consular tourist visas have always required — but the list of eligible nationalities has not been published, so for now the advance-visa rule still stands and the portal is a channel to watch, not yet a settled route.
title: Turkmenistan launches an e-Visa portal
Colombia's visa exemption for Israel restored
summary: After the 2024-2026 diplomatic break, Colombia's ordinary-passport exemption was restored 1 September 2026 (embassy confirmation reported 3 September); Colombians again travel on ETA-IL for up to 90 days.
source_name: Wikipedia - Visa policy of Israel (current exemption table)

title: Mauritania's visa-free access to Libya restored
summary: Mauritania's ordinary-passport holders are again visa-free for Libya for up to 3 months, restored on 30 August 2026 and back on the Timatic-based exemption table; visa-free entry is limited to landing at Tripoli Mitiga and Misurata airports, and a security letter from the Libyan immigration authorities may be required.
source_name: Visa policy of Libya (Timatic-based table; North Africa News, 4 September 2026)

title: Morocco lifts the visa requirement for Albanian citizens
summary: From 15 August 2026, Albanian ordinary-passport holders are visa-free for short stays in Morocco, notified by Morocco's embassy in Rome to Albania's Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, implementing the 1 March 2025 joint declaration. The announcement did not state a maximum stay; 90 days is the short-stay ceiling in Morocco's Law No. 02-03 carried in pair data.
source_name: Albania Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs — exemption announcement (August 2026)
South Africa Electronic Travel Authorisation (DHA)
summary: South Africa switched on its Electronic Travel Authorisation for nationals of China, India, Indonesia and Mexico — initially only for air arrivals at OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria airports. The ETA is multiple-entry with stays of up to 90 days. Everyone else still follows the exemption table or needs a visa in advance; there is no visa on arrival.
title: South Africa's ETA goes live for four nationalities
Cairo airport digital visa on arrival
summary: Cairo International Airport begins selling a digital QR visa on arrival (US$36 including a US$6 service fee) via self-service machines and the Visa on Arrival portal, alongside the US$30 paper sticker. The Washington embassy later claims all airports moved to QR from 1 September 2026, against GOV.UK's Cairo-only account — the scope is unresolved.
source_name: GOV.UK — Egypt travel advice
Cabo Verde government portal (gov.cv)
summary: Every traveller to Cabo Verde must pre-register on the EASE portal and pay the airport security tax (TSA, 3,400 CVE online). Since 1 July 2026, arriving without proof of pre-registration costs double the TSA at the border. Pre-registration is an immigration formality, not a visa — it changes nothing about who needs a visa.
title: Cabo Verde doubles the airport tax for unregistered arrivals

source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Armenia
summary: A government decree temporarily exempts nationals of 111 countries who hold a valid residence permit from the US, the EU, the Schengen area or a GCC state. The measure runs from 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027. It is residence-based, not passport-based — an ordinary passport alone does not qualify.
title: Armenia temporarily exempts residence-permit holders of 111 countries
Malaysia becomes visa-free for Libya for 30 days
summary: Malaysian ordinary-passport holders are visa-free for Libya for up to 30 days from 8 June 2026, limited to landing at Tripoli Mitiga and Misurata airports, with a possible security-letter requirement. Malaysia's own older visa table still shows Libya as visa-required and has not been updated for this change.
source_name: Visa policy of Libya (Timatic-based table; Libya Herald, 24 June 2026)
Voyage Togo — official travel platform
summary: A decree adopted by Togo's Council of Ministers on 26 May 2026 exempts nationals of every African state holding a valid passport from entry visas for stays of up to 30 days. Exempt travellers still file a free travel declaration on the Togo Voyage platform at least 24 hours before arrival. Non-African travellers still need the platform's e-Visa in advance — visas on arrival were abolished in 2022.
title: Togo exempts all African nationals for 30 days

source_name: Sri Lanka ETA portal
summary: Under Special Gazette No. 2490/02, Sri Lanka's ETA became free of charge for nationals of 40 countries, on top of the long-standing bilateral free list. The system is unchanged otherwise: everyone applies for an ETA (online, or at the Colombo airport counter) and receives a 30-day double-entry visit pass.
title: Sri Lanka makes the ETA free for 40 countries

source_name: Saudi Press Agency
summary: The Saudi–Russian mutual exemption agreement took effect on 11 May 2026: ordinary passports of both countries now get 90 days visa-free. The e-Visa portal's eligibility pages lagged behind the announcement, which is why many datasets still show Russia as e-Visa only.
title: Saudi Arabia and Russia switch on mutual visa-free travel

source_name: Boletim Oficial n.º 14, II Série — Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026
summary: Interior Ministry Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026 (Boletim Oficial n.º 14, II Série, 23 January 2026) lists 91 nationalities who must hold a visa before travelling — entry, transit and airport stopovers without one are refused. Nationalities on neither that annex nor the exempt table keep the border visa. Holders of EU/EEA, UK, Swiss, Brazilian, Canadian or US residence permits are carved out of the advance-visa duty even if their passport is listed.
title: Cabo Verde moves 91 nationalities to advance-visa-only

source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali
summary: By Foreign Ministry communiqués of 30 December 2025 and 2 January 2026, Mali suspended the entry of US ordinary-passport holders entirely from 1 January 2026, citing reciprocity. The measure is framed as reciprocal and not necessarily permanent; the US embassy's older fee and validity pages predate it and no longer apply.
title: Mali suspends entry for US citizens
Lebanon quadruples visit-visa fees
summary: Under the 2026 Budget Law, General Security raised the visit/tourist entry-visa fee from 500,000 LBP to 2,000,000 LBP on 18 February 2026; work-entry, conversion and sponsor-transfer fees were set to the same 2,000,000 LBP. Port-issued tourist visas themselves stay free — the fee bites on pre-approved/consular visas and on in-country extensions. Old dollar prices still shown on some embassy pages (USD 17/35) are pre-reform leftovers.
source_name: Lebanese General Security, visa types and fees
Cabinet Resolution No. 855 (Ministry of Justice database)
summary: Cabinet Resolution No. 855 of 31 December 2025 rewrote the stay arithmetic: the 55-country visa-free regime that read as '60 days' now means 30 days within any 60-day period, Gulf-state nationals get 180 days within 360, and EAEU and several bilateral partners sit at 90-in-180. The headline number most datasets show is no longer the operative one.
title: Kyrgyzstan cuts visa-free stays in a New Year's Eve reform

source_name: Agence Nigérienne de Presse (ANP)
summary: An official communiqué of 25 December 2025 announced a complete and indefinite halt to issuing visas to US citizens and to their entry into Niger, citing reciprocity. Unlike a suspension with a review date, no end condition has been published.
title: Niger bars US citizens indefinitely
Algeria grants 14-day visa-free access to Hong Kong SAR passport holders
summary: From 25 November 2025, Hong Kong SAR passport holders may visit Algeria visa-free for up to 14 days, on notification from the Algerian government to the Hong Kong government. Some airline check-in systems were slow to reflect the arrangement. Algeria still publishes no consolidated exemption list; its ordinary-passport exemptions remain a short list (Libya, Malaysia, Mali, Mauritania, Seychelles, Tunisia at 90 days).
source_name: Government of the Hong Kong SAR — visa-free access announcement (25 November 2025)
eVisaburkina — official e-Visa portal
summary: A cabinet decision of 11 September 2025 waived visa fees for nationals of all African states. The application itself is still required — Burkinabè visas run through the eVisaburkina portal with central approval — but the fee line for African passports dropped to zero.
title: Burkina Faso waives visa fees for all African citizens

source_name: Somalia Immigration and Citizenship Agency
summary: From 1 September 2025, all foreign nationals must apply online in advance through Somalia's e-Visa/eTAS portal — the Immigration and Citizenship Agency's launch notice ended walk-up issuance for ordinary passports. The widely publicised waivers for a handful of countries turned out to cover diplomatic and official passports only.
title: Somalia makes the advance e-Visa mandatory for everyone
Nigeria launches the e-Visa and abolishes visas on arrival
summary: From 1 May 2025 every traveller who needs a visa for Nigeria must obtain an e-Visa at evisa.immigration.gov.ng before travel; the visa-on-arrival system was abolished the same day. The standard short-visit e-Visa (tourism F5A, single-entry business F4A) is valid for 90 days from issuance and allows a single stay of up to 30 days, non-extendable. ECOWAS citizens and Cameroonians and Chadians remain visa-free, and every traveller must file the free electronic Landing Card before arrival.
source_name: Nigeria Immigration Service — Tourism Visa (F5A) page
Namibia MHAISS — Visa Fact Sheet v4
summary: From 1 April 2025 Namibia replaced its long-standing exemption practice with a reciprocity-based system: a short visa-free list (90 days), a long visa-on-arrival list (fees differ for African Union and non-AU nationals), and everyone else on an advance e-Visa. Several nationalities that had entered freely for decades now need a visa.
title: Namibia rebuilds its visa regime on reciprocity

source_name: Liberia Immigration Service — Visa on Arrival portal
summary: Since 11 March 2025, Liberia's visa on arrival exists only as an online pre-approval: apply at least 7 days ahead on the Liberia Immigration Service portal, pay US$102.50, and collect the sticker after biometrics at Roberts International Airport. There is no walk-up arrival visa, and travellers resident in a country with a Liberian embassy must use the embassy instead.
title: Liberia moves its airport visa to mandatory online pre-approval
Mauritania makes the e-Visa mandatory and abolishes visas on arrival
summary: From 5 January 2025 every traveller who needs a visa for Mauritania must obtain an e-Visa from the ANRPTS portal (anrpts.gov.mr) before boarding; the walk-up visa on arrival was abolished and Mauritanian embassies have since stopped issuing visas altogether. The fee is paid in cash on arrival (from €40 / $45 for 30 days for Arab and African nationals, €55 / $60 for other nationalities). Eleven nationalities — including Senegal, Mali, Niger, Algeria, Tunisia and Libya — remain visa-free under mutual abolition agreements.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mauritania — visa page
